Growing together in wisdom, stature and favour - Luke 2:52
Growing together in wisdom, stature and favour
"Pupils' spiritual development is excellent. They embrace the strong sense of Christian fellowship and community in the school, reflect on their own experiences and translate them into a palpable sense of service to those around them... Pupils seek opportunities to translate their faith into action, thus fulfilling the vison of the school's leadership to encourage its pupils to make a positive difference to the world."‍ISI Report, January 2023
God is firmly at the centre of all that we do, allowing children to develop a strong sense of identity and destiny, secure in who they are and look confidently to the future.
The King’s School is a unique environment in which children from Reception to Year 11 can thrive and grow both spiritually and academically.
Wisdom
While delivering a broad and balanced curriculum we ensure that all our learning is placed within a distinctive Christian context, enabling pupils to view the world through a God-centred lens.
Stature
We place great value on developing character, giving opportunities for our pupils to grow in confidence and independence, while being encouraged to aim high and fulfil their potential.
Favour
The Bible teaches us to love God and each other. At The King’s School we provide an environment in which pupils can develop their relationship with God and develop their inter personal skills.
Excellent learning environment
We provide a peaceful, secure and happy environment, which enables pupils to make excellent academic progress. Our small class sizes ensure that every pupil is known and valued and that their individual needs can be met, stretching and supporting as appropriate.

Senior
Senior curriculum
Christ-centred education
Teaching young people the truth about God and His world is at the centre of Christian education. As our senior pupils progress through the school they gain a deepening awareness of God’s plans and purposes for their lives
The content of a Christian curriculum will not be vastly different from that seen as the standard curriculum taught in most schools today. It is the context within which that content is placed which makes the difference.
Christian education derives its context and basis from truth and values taught by God through the Bible. In our secure environment, where achievement at every level is encouraged and supported, pupils engage in a structured programme of academic and spiritual challenge.‍
Key Stage 3
Key Stage 3 provides a broad and balanced curriculum, offering experience in a wide range of different traditional subject areas, while also giving plenty of room to developing pupils’ creative gifting.
Personal, Social and Health Education
Key Stage 4
Pupils at The King’s School are prepared for up to 11 GCSE subjects. These are drawn from a broad range of disciplines in order to establish a balanced education and prepare pupils for further and higher education.
The GCSE programme comprises a number of core subjects and also allows pupils to choose from a selection of other subjects.

Senior
Senior enrichment
Enrichment activities are an integral part of the life of The King’s School, providing pupils with opportunities to enhance their personal development, extend their learning experience beyond the classroom and into the wider community and develop expertise in areas beyond the formal curriculum. Enrichment activities include visiting speakers, theatre visits, lunchtime and after school clubs, trips and sporting activities. These opportunities enable pupils to have fun together, cultivate great friendships, make enduring memories, and learn many important life skills.
Some of the activities which senior pupils have enjoyed have included watersports, trips to Paulton’s Park and Thorpe Park as well as in house enrichment days where pupils are able to develop their skills in a chosen area of interest such as cookery, textiles or drama. Theatre trips are part of the curriculum for GCSE Drama and pupils are encouraged to attend theatre performances of English Literature set texts. The English Department also runs a debating club, competing successfully against other schools. Other departments run subject specific trips throughout the year such as Geography field trips and History trips to London.‍
‍Sports Clubs, Competitions and Fixtures
Our new multi use games area (MUGA) enables pupils to participate in a wide range of sporting activities. Throughout the year, the P.E. department organises a variety of after school sporting clubs including football, netball, tennis and athletics. Pupils have the opportunity to compete against other schools both home and away.‍
Music and Drama Clubs
The Music and Drama Departments regularly organise a range of extra-curricular opportunities for pupils to participate in various activities including school productions and national events. Over the years they have included Rock Challenge, Young Voices, The Southampton Music Festival and whole school productions such as The Man who Was Magic, Wendy and Peter Pan. and The Lion, The Witch and the Wardrobe.
‍‍GCSE Booster Classes
Every year teachers run after school booster classes which are open to pupils keen to supplement their studies and better prepare for the GCSE examinations.
Skiing
The school runs a bi-annual ski trip, usually to France or Italy, which is open to pupils in Years 8 to 11. Pupils who have not skied before, or who need a refresher course, will have the opportunity to have lessons at the Alpine Centre, Southampton.
Work experience
In the Summer Term Year 10 pupils participate in an internal work experience programme, run by the school, providing pupils with the opportunity of developing marketing, budgeting and presentational skills within a team environment. They engage in activities which are designed to help them learn about the world of work, develop practical and interpersonal skills and grow in confidence. Pupils benefit from taking on new roles and responsibilities and also find direction on future college and career choices.

pageCache.text:
About us
Alumni & Supporters
At The King’s School, our legacy is built on the memories and achievements of our past pupils, staff, parents and supporters, and all God has done and continues to do in your lives.
We invite you to stay connected with us as valued members of our extended family. By joining our mailing list you will receive our new supporters newsletter. This annual publication contains updates from The King’s School and opportunities to engage with our vibrant school community. Whether you're looking to reconnect with old friends, support current pupils, or simply stay informed about our initiatives, we're thrilled to welcome you back and keep The King's School community thriving.
We can only keep in touch with your permission, so please take a few moments to complete your details below to join our mailing list and receive our Alumni and Supporters Newsletter.
History of The King's School
In 1982, a young Christian teacher with a big vision, decided to leave the security of state school teaching and, together with a few friends and their children, set up The King’s School.
40 years later, we are a thriving independent school with exams results recognised as 'extraordinary' by our recent ISI inspection.
Over the past 40 years we have seen God's provision and blessing over The King's School, its staff and pupils. We look forward with expectation to what God will do over the next 40 years and beyond.
"Jesus Christ is the same yesterday and today and forever."
The King’s School has been making a difference to young people's lives for more than 40 years.
Useful information
We offer a range of lunchtime clubs for both primary and senior pupils and a range of different after school music and sports clubs. Seniors benefit from after school GCSE Revision clubs from the Spring Term onwards.
Parents can book their children into breakfast club from 8.00am and after school club until 4.30pm on a weekly basis. Sessions can be booked via our school shop. Senior pupils may arrive on site from 8.00am and stay until 4.30pm (parental consent required for all after school activities). Parents must let us know in advance if they need to pick up their children later than 4.30pm.
There is no requirement for prospective pupils to complete an entrance exam. However, we do not offer vocational courses in the senior school and pupils must be able to access the GCSE curriculum across a range of subjects.
We do not have school buses but the school is well served by local transport networks. Parents often organise their own lift shares.
We have very limited parking onsite. St Swithun’s Wells Catholic Church very kindly allow us to use their car park for pick up and drop off only for Primary parents. We ask Senior parents to park considerately in neighbouring roads further away from the school. When dropping your child off please park without blocking or obstructing any property or access routes owned by residents. We value the new community that has grown around our school and are keen to develop positive relationships with those living nearby.
Most pupils bring in a packed lunch but we offer a limited lunch service of sandwiches, jacket potatoes and pasta salad which pupils can order on a daily basis. Parents are invoiced accordingly.

About us
Headteacher's welcome
Choosing the right school for your child is one of the most important decisions that you will ever have to make. Children spend a considerable amount of their time in school and, just as every child is unique, each school is also different. At The King’s School we provide a nurturing Christian environment in which children can thrive and grow both spiritually and academically. Here childhood is valued and treasured and God is firmly at the centre of all that we do.
Having both primary and senior pupils on one site facilitates a strong sense of family, encouraging positive relationships between staff, parents and pupils. The King's School is a peaceful, secure and happy place where children are encouraged to have high aspirations and to treat others with kindness and respect. Our small class sizes ensure that every pupil is known and valued and that their individual needs can be met. There are many opportunities for children to develop their gifts and abilities and grow in confidence and character.
This has been a particularly exciting season in the life of The King’s School. Not only did we celebrate 40 years of God’s faithfulness and provision in 2022, but we also completed our new Multi Use Games Area (MUGA) which has transformed our PE lessons and break times for our pupils. And if that were not exciting enough, we are now planning a new two storey Primary building to replace the existing portacabins.
While continually improving our facilities is important, this is not our main priority. Our prayer is that throughout their time at The King’s School children will grow in their faith, knowing that God loves them and has a plan for their life, and that by the time they leave the school they are well equipped for all that lies ahead and able to make a positive difference in the world.
If you have not yet had the opportunity to visit, please contact the office to arrange an appointment. I would be delighted to meet you personally and take you on a tour of our unique school.
Caroline Santer, Headteacher

Primary curriculum
Christ-centred education
Teaching children the truth about God and His world is at the centre of Christian education.
Although the content of a Christian curriculum is not vastly different from that taught in most schools today, it is the context within which that content is placed that makes the difference. Christian education derives its context and basis from truths and values taught by God through the Bible. Each class focusses on a half termly Heart Concept, a Bible verse or Biblical truth, around which all their other learning is based.
Although numeracy and literacy are a key focus, a broad range of other subjects are highly valued, allowing pupils to discover their own areas of interest and enjoyment.
Small class sizes enable us to meet the needs of all pupils as teachers know each child well, supporting them as individuals in their learning journey.
Reception
The Early Years Foundation Stage (EYFS) that is taught in Reception is a continuation of a child’s learning journey from nursery and/ or pre-school. Throughout the year there is a mixture of child-initiated activities and adult-directed tasks. Secure relationships and an enabling environment are crucial to allow individual children to thrive in all areas of development. Activities are designed to allow opportunities for children to progress in the 3 Characteristics of Effective Learning as well as the 17 Early Learning Goals that are outlined below.

Being willing to ‘have a go’

Admissions
School fees 2026/27
Our fees include textbooks, stationery, chromebooks (Y7 upwards), off-site visits and trips, including residential visits and entry for external examinations. A detailed list of what is included can be viewed in the notes below, or for a full list click here: what do fees include
Fees are subject to an annual increase by the Trustees each September. A full term's notice in writing, or payment in lieu of notice, is required before withdrawal of a pupil. Click here for the full Terms and Conditions.
Multi-year Agreements
To give families certainty over their payments we are pleased to be able to offer multi-year agreements, where the monthly fee is fixed* for the duration of the agreement.
Length of Agreement (Years)
(* there are separate terms and conditions that apply to these agreements)
Annual Fee Agreements
Annual Fee Agreements are published every year and you should expect an annual inflationary increase of 5%.
To discuss which option is best for your and your family, please email our Finance Team to arrange a phone call.
Notes
A sibling discount is available once two or more of your children are in Year 7-11. At present it is a 20% reduction in fees for the eldest child.
Annual fees have to be paid on or before 31st August as the academic year starts on the 1st September.
Monthly fees are via Direct Debit and are for the 12 monthly payments starting on the 1st September. From 2027-2028, the fees for Year 11 will be paid over 10 months so that all fees are settled by the time the pupil leaves the school.
What is not included:
The School has a Fees in Advance scheme, please contact the Finance Team for a personal quotation.

'Pupils work together highly effectively and make positive contributions to the life of the school.' ISI Report, January 2023
School life
Pastoral care
Children spend a significant amount of their life at school and we ensure that all our pupils feel secure when they are in our care. Pastoral support is a strength at The King’s School; teachers prioritise building positive relationships with their classes and pray for them regularly.
In primary the main level of pastoral support is provided by class teachers. With small class sizes teachers have the opportunity to know each child individually, understanding not only their strengths and weaknesses, but also their joys and concerns. They have time to listen to each child and support them during their time in school as they develop both academically and in character.
Pastoral care in the senior part of the school is provided initially by form tutors, and is overseen by the Pastoral Leads. Each day begins with a devotional tutor time. This allows opportunity for tutors to get alongside the pupils in their group, developing relationships and getting to know them as individuals. Our Learning Support Team is available for those who require additional support.
Parents are always welcome to come and talk to teachers and tutors as we work together to best support every child.

About us
Results
“Pupils achieve good and sometimes excellent learning outcomes across the school from a diverse range of starting points…… Many of their results in optional subjects and religious studies, which are taken before Year 11, are above expectation...[and] routinely perform above their predicted levels, often by more than a grade.”
ISI Report, January 2023
Pupils at The King’s School take GCSE examinations for core subjects in Year 11: English Language, English Literature, Mathematics, Science (either Triple or Combined) and either Spanish or Geography.
Year 10 pupils take GCSE Religious Studies.
Option subjects are taken by a combination of Year 9, 10 & 11 pupils. These include:Art, Child Development, Citizenship, Computer Science, Drama, Food & Nutrition, History, Music, Physical Education and Textiles

The King’s School has been making a difference to young people's lives for more than 40 years.
Useful information
We offer a range of lunchtime clubs for both primary and senior pupils and a range of different after school music and sports clubs. Seniors benefit from after school GCSE Revision clubs from the Spring Term onwards.
Parents can book their children into breakfast club from 8.00am and after school club until 4.30pm on a weekly basis. Sessions can be booked via our school shop. Senior pupils may arrive on site from 8.00am and stay until 4.30pm (parental consent required for all after school activities). Parents must let us know in advance if they need to pick up their children later than 4.30pm.
There is no requirement for prospective pupils to complete an entrance exam. However, we do not offer vocational courses in the senior school and pupils must be able to access the GCSE curriculum across a range of subjects.
We do not have school buses but the school is well served by local transport networks. Parents often organise their own lift shares.
We have very limited parking onsite. St Swithun’s Wells Catholic Church very kindly allow us to use their car park for pick up and drop off only for Primary parents. We ask Senior parents to park considerately in neighbouring roads further away from the school. When dropping your child off please park without blocking or obstructing any property or access routes owned by residents. We value the new community that has grown around our school and are keen to develop positive relationships with those living nearby.
Most pupils bring in a packed lunch but we offer a limited lunch service of sandwiches, jacket potatoes and pasta salad which pupils can order on a daily basis. Parents are invoiced accordingly.
